'''Lynn G. Schreyer''' (formerly '''Lynn Laverne Schreyer Bennethum''') is an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] whose research concerns the [[mathematical model]]ing of [[porous media]]. She is associate professor of mathematics and statistics at [[Washington State University]], and full professor of the department of mathematics and statistics at Washington State University in March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lynn Schreyer |url=http://math.wsu.edu/faculty/lschreyer/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190117112436/http://math.wsu.edu/faculty/lschreyer/ |archive-date=2019-01-17 |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Department of Mathematics and Statistics at Washington State University |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Lynn Schreyer |url=https://math.wsu.edu/faculty/wsu-profile/lynn.schreyer/ |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Department of Mathematics and Statistics, Washington State University}}</ref> Schreyer server as chair of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] Activity Group on Geosciences from 2004 to 2006.<ref name=siag>{{citation|url=http://wiki.siam.org/siag-gs/index.php/Officers|title=Officers|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics Activity Group on Geosciences|accessdate=2021-01-10}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Schreyer studied [[mechanical engineering]] at the [[University of New Mexico]], graduating ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]'' in 1986. After earning a [[master's degree]] in mechanical engineering at [[Northwestern University]] in 1988, she switched to mathematics, earning a second master's degree in 1990 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1994, both from [[Purdue University]].<ref name="vita">{{cite web |date=Feb 2022 |title=Curriculum vitae |url=http://math.wsu.edu/faculty/lschreyer/vita_web.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130134536/https://math.wsu.edu/faculty/lschreyer/vita_web.pdf#gsc.tab=0 |archive-date=2022-11-30 |accessdate= |website=Washington State University Department of Mathematics}}</ref> Her dissertation, ''Multiscale Hybrid Mixture Theory for Swelling Systems with Interfaces'', was jointly supervised by Jim Douglas Jr. and John H. Cushman.<ref name=gene>{{mathgenealogy|id=16531}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research in [[agronomy]] at Purdue, Schreyer became an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of Colorado Denver]], earning tenure there as an associate professor in 2002. She moved to her present position at Washington State University in 2016.<ref name=vita />

Schreyer chaired the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) Activity Group on Geosciences (SIAG-GS) from 2004 to 2006.<ref name=siag />
